title: Sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices, skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among Malaysian national-level outdoor athletes
title_original: Sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices, skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among Malaysian national-level outdoor athletes
summary: Outdoor athletes in equatorial regions are exposed to high levels of ultraviolet (UV) radiation year-round, increasing the risk of cumulative photodamage. However, evidence on sun protection behaviours and personal UVB exposure among athletes in tropical settings remains limited. This study assessed sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP), skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among national-level outdoor athletes in Malaysia. Skin pigmentation was objectively measured using spectrophotometry, while personal UVB exposure was quantified using polysulphone film badges. Male athletes were predominantly classified within the darker ITA-based skin colour categories and had greater exposed body surface area than female athletes during training and non-training periods. UVB exposure differed significantly across sporting disciplines, with sailing athletes recording the highest daily exposure (3.5 ± 1.2 SED/day). Female athletes had higher attitude scores than male athletes (79.8 ± 8.2% vs. 74.1 ± 8.8%; P = 0.003). title: Reconciling Strict Liability and Proportionality in Anti-Doping Law: A Two-Stage Framework for Athlete Protection in Indonesia
title_original: Reconciling Strict Liability and Proportionality in Anti-Doping Law: A Two-Stage Framework for Athlete Protection in Indonesia
summary: Anti-doping policy aims to protect the integrity of sport, but the strict liability principle under the World Anti-Doping Code may raise concerns about the legal protection of athletes. The research problem lies in the absence of a national framework that clearly distinguishes between establishing an anti-doping rule violation and determining the appropriate sanction, as well as the lack of protective infrastructure that enables Indonesian athletes to access the proportionality mechanisms provided by the Code. The study employs a juridical-empirical (socio-legal) method combining statutory, conceptual, comparative, and empirical approaches, based on interviews with stakeholders and participatory observation. The findings show that Indonesia’s normative framework is largely aligned with the Code. The main challenges lie in implementation, including funding dependence, limited testing capacity, low levels of athlete awareness, inadequate legal assistance, and a mismatch between BPOM product authorization and the Prohibited List. Strict liability remains justified at the stage of establishing a violation, whereas proportionality should operate at the fault-based stage of determining the sanction. The article recommends a two-stage framework for athlete protection, supported by an institutional layer comprising IADO–BPOM coordination, legal assistance, and greater IADO independence.

title: Neuromuscular fatigue induces phase-specific multisegmental kinematic adaptations in elite traditional rowers: a three-dimensional analysis
title_original: Neuromuscular fatigue induces phase-specific multisegmental kinematic adaptations in elite traditional rowers: a three-dimensional analysis
summary: Introduction Neuromuscular fatigue disrupts rowing technique, yet its multisegmental effects in Traditional fixed-seat rowing remain poorly understood. This study examined the phase-specific impact of fatigue on joint angles, body segment heights, and center of gravity position at the catch and finish phases. Methods Nineteen elite male Traditional rowers (age: 29.4 ± 7.0 years, height: 182.0 ± 6.1 cm, body mass: 78.2 ± 8.0 kg) competing in the ACT, the highest Traditional rowing league division, were recruited for a within-subject pre–post design; two did not complete the post-fatigue assessment and marker availability varied, so paired analyses included ≤17 complete cases per variable. Following a pre-fatigue kinematic assessment, participants performed a standardized incremental test to volitional exhaustion on a fixed-seat ergometer. Three-dimensional kinematic data were captured using an STT Systems 3DMA. Paired-samples t -tests compared pre- and post-fatigue conditions, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons and Cohen's d as effect size. Results Body segment heights decreased significantly after fatigue and remained significant after correction. At the catch, head (1,182.0 vs. 1,163.8 mm), shoulder (914.3 vs. 882.9 mm) and hand heights (641.1 vs. 626.9 mm) were reduced (adjusted p ≤ 0.042; d = −0.72 to −1.19); at the finish, head (1,073.7 vs. 1,049.0 mm) and hand heights (989.3 vs. 962.8 mm) were reduced (adjusted p = 0.024; d = −0.78 and −0.79). The vertical center of gravity decreased at both the catch (659.4 vs. 647.9 mm; adjusted p = 0.045; d = −0.64) and finish (565.2 vs. 551.5 mm; adjusted p = 0.045; d = −0.64). Changes in joint angulations (increased shoulder and elbow flexion, decreased knee flexion) showed unadjusted trends but did not survive correction and are reported as exploratory. Conclusion Neuromuscular fatigue induces distinct, phase-specific kinematic adaptations in Traditional rowing, characterized by a systematic reduction in postural height (all three upper-body landmarks at the catch, and head and hand heights at the finish) and exploratory joint-angle adjustments at the catch and finish. These findings support multisegmental three-dimensional kinematic analysis as a sensitive tool for monitoring fatigue-related technique changes in Traditional rowing, with implications for training design and potential relevance for injury prevention.

title: Tradução e adaptação transcultural do sport mental toughness questionnaire para a língua portuguesa do Brasil
title_original: Tradução e adaptação transcultural do sport mental toughness questionnaire para a língua portuguesa do Brasil
summary: O vigor mental (mental toughness) é um construto amplamente associado ao desempenho esportivo, sendo considerado um importante preditor da capacidade de atletas lidarem com pressão, adversidade e demandas competitivas. Apesar de sua relevância, a avaliação desse construto no contexto brasileiro é limitada pela escassez de instrumentos psicometricamente adequados e culturalmente adaptados. O presente estudo teve como objetivo traduzir e realizar a adaptação transcultural do Sport Mental Toughness Questionnaire (SMTQ) para o português do Brasil. O processo incluiu tradução independente, síntese das versões, retrotradução, avaliação por comitê de especialistas e pré-teste com atletas. A versão final do instrumento, denominada Questionário de Vigor Mental no Esporte, apresentou adequada equivalência semântica, idiomática, conceitual e cultural. O pré-teste indicou boa compreensibilidade dos itens e aceitabilidade pelo público-alvo. Conclui-se que a versão brasileira do SMTQ apresenta evidências iniciais de validade de conteúdo e adequação cultural, sendo necessária a condução de estudos adicionais para investigação de suas propriedades psicométricas, incluindo validade de construto e confiabilidade.

title: Scaphoid Fractures in Athletes: Diagnostic Pitfalls and Return-to-Sport Strategies - a narrative review
title_original: Scaphoid Fractures in Athletes: Diagnostic Pitfalls and Return-to-Sport Strategies - a narrative review
summary: Background. The scaphoid is the most frequently fractured carpal bone and is disproportionately common in athletes exposed to falls on an outstretched hand or direct impact to the wrist. Its retrograde, predominantly distal-to-proximal blood supply makes the fracture prone to diagnostic delay, nonunion, and avascular necrosis, while the athlete's imperative to return quickly to competition creates persistent tension between imaging accuracy, treatment choice, and timing of return to sport.Aim. To synthesise, critically and comparatively, the diagnostic pathway, treatment options, and return-to-sport considerations for scaphoid fractures in athletic populations, with emphasis on the medical rationale behind imaging strategies, operative versus conservative management, and their documented functional consequences.Materials and Methods. This narrative review draws on peer-reviewed epidemiological studies, cohort series, randomised controlled trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, diagnostic accuracy studies, artificial-intelligence validation studies, biomechanical studies, and international consensus statements.Results. Diagnostic accuracy varies substantially across radiography, CT, MRI, bone scintigraphy, ultrasound, cone-beam CT and artificial-intelligence-assisted reading, with important trade-offs in sensitivity, specificity, cost, and time to diagnosis. Surgical fixation generally accelerates radiographic union and return to sport relative to cast immobilisation, but the evidence for superior long-term functional outcomes is inconsistent, and nonunion, smoking status, and fracture displacement modify these effects.Conclusions. Optimal management of the athlete with a suspected or confirmed scaphoid fracture requires individualised integration of imaging accuracy, fracture stability, sport-specific demands, and rigorously defined return-to-sport criteria, rather than a uniform diagnostic or therapeutic algorithm.

title: Legal and Ethical Challenges in Age Verification in Indian Sports: A Critical Analysis of Chronological and Biological Standards
title_original: Legal and Ethical Challenges in Age Verification in Indian Sports: A Critical Analysis of Chronological and Biological Standards
summary: Age verification is a long-standing challenge in Indian sports, especially in age-group competitions where fairness and equal opportunity are essential. India currently follows the National Code Against Age Fraud in Sports, which relies mainly on dental and radiological examinations to determine an athlete’s chronological age. However, these methods do not consider variations in biological age, which can differ significantly due to nutrition, training exposure, genetics and socio-economic background. As a result, many young athletes face incorrect classification, unfair exclusion and unequal competition environments. In contrast, several international sports bodies have adopted more scientific and athlete-centred approaches. FIFA employs MRI-based wrist assessment to evaluate bone maturity in U-17 tournaments, while countries in Europe and East Asia integrate skeletal maturity indicators, growth-tracking data and long-term athlete development (LTAD) models. These systems acknowledge that two athletes of the same chronological age may not share the same physiological development, and therefore provide a more accurate and welfare-oriented assessment process. This study uses a comparative legal and policy analysis approach to examine India’s current age-verification framework alongside global best practices. It argues that accurate age assessment is essential not only for competition integrity, a key component of clean sport, but also for athlete safety, as biologically younger athletes may face increased physical and psychological risks when competing against more mature peers. The paper proposes adopting a phased, multi-factor assessment model for India that includes bone maturity tests, growth-monitoring mechanisms and standardised medical guidelines supported by sports science. Such reforms would reduce disputes, improve transparency and promote athlete welfare. The study concludes that modernising India’s age-verification system in line with international standards is vital for strengthening fairness, safeguarding young athletes and advancing the broader goals of clean and safe sport in the country.

title: Mechanical and Friction-Induced Dermatoses in Athletes: Black Heel, Piezogenic Papules, and Related Traumatic Skin Conditions - a narrative review
title_original: Mechanical and Friction-Induced Dermatoses in Athletes: Black Heel, Piezogenic Papules, and Related Traumatic Skin Conditions - a narrative review
summary: Background. Repetitive mechanical loading, shear, and friction in sport produce a recognisable spectrum of cutaneous injuries frequently mistaken for infectious, neoplastic, or systemic disease. Black heel (talon noir), piezogenic pedal papules, blisters, calluses, corns, jogger's toe, and subungual haematoma are common but underreported, and their mimicry of acral melanoma creates diagnostic risk.Aim. To synthesise the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnostic pitfalls, and management of mechanical and friction-induced dermatoses in athletes, with emphasis on black heel and piezogenic papules.Materials and Methods. This narrative review draws on peer-reviewed epidemiological surveys, hospital and sports-cohort case series, dermatological case reports, a paediatric scoping review, biomechanical and finite-element modelling studies, and consensus reviews of sports dermatology, connective tissue disease, and skin barrier physiology.Results. Friction-related lesions cluster on the feet, hands, and trunk and are associated with running distance, footwear, surface, and training volume. Talon noir and piezogenic papules are usually benign and self-limited, but can mimic acral lentiginous melanoma or signal connective tissue disorders such as Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, GATA2 deficiency, or joint hypermobility, particularly when lesions are painful, atypical, or occur outside the expected age or activity context. Diagnostic accuracy improves with dermoscopy, scraping tests, and attention to bilateral distribution and exertion history. Management is predominantly conservative, though intralesional therapies exist for refractory painful piezogenic papules.Conclusions. Awareness of the mechanical aetiology and differential diagnosis of these dermatoses can reduce unnecessary biopsies and psychological burden while ensuring that rare but important systemic associations are not overlooked.

title: Music engagement, nutrition strategies, and psychological well-being in competitive athletes: a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study
title_original: Music engagement, nutrition strategies, and psychological well-being in competitive athletes: a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study
summary: Competitive athletes routinely face psychological demands that intersect with daily behavioral practices, yet music engagement and nutrition strategies have rarely been examined together as correlates of athlete psychological well-being. This study investigated the cross-sectional associations of strategic music use and differentiated nutrition strategies with a psychological well-being and recovery-related mental state composite among competitive athletes, using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design. Survey data were collected from 350 competitive athletes in Changsha, China, between February and May 2026, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 purposively selected participants. Measurement validity was evaluated through exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and associations were estimated using multiple regression and structural equation modeling while adjusting for demographic and training covariates. Music engagement was positively associated with the psychological well-being composite ( β = 0.31, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.41, p < 0.001), and nutrition strategies showed a comparably stronger association ( β = 0.39, 95% CI 0.30 to 0.49, p < 0.001). Qualitative interviews indicated that athletes used music intentionally for arousal regulation, focus, and emotional recovery, while hydration and meal regularity were perceived as more feasible than diet planning, which was constrained by travel, scheduling, and resource barriers. These findings suggest that strategic music use and consistent nutrition practices represent behavioral correlates of athlete-reported psychological functioning and may inform non-clinical, athlete-centered self-management approaches, though longitudinal and intervention research is needed to evaluate directionality and causal mechanisms.

title: Potential Contamination Cases in Anti‐Doping: Experiences and Practices of 33 Anti‐Doping Organisations
title_original: Potential Contamination Cases in Anti‐Doping: Experiences and Practices of 33 Anti‐Doping Organisations
summary: Unintentional doping, the inadvertent ingestion of or exposure to substances on the World Anti-Doping Agency's Prohibited List, is an increasing concern in sport, with potential sources ranging from dietary supplements and contaminated foods to pharmaceuticals, intimate contact, and the wider environment. When an adverse analytical finding (AAF) is reported, Anti-Doping Organisations (ADOs) must distinguish doping from inadvertent exposure, a task that carries real consequences for athletes' careers. Yet little is known about how ADOs handle such cases in practice. Through the Monitoring Group of the Council of Europe's Anti-Doping Convention, we conducted an electronic survey of National Anti-Doping Organisations and International Federations on their experiences and practices for managing potential contamination cases during 2024-2025. Thirty-three ADOs, predominantly from Europe, responded. The majority (85%) had encountered at least one contamination case during the period, yet only 36% had a standardised process for handling such cases. Athletes claiming contamination, however, were rarely successful in defending their case. ADOs reported 46 unique prohibited substances and 71 source-substance associations being involved in alleged contamination cases, with dietary supplements the most frequent source (76%), followed by food (42%). Adoption of standardised processes increased with the operational scale of the ADO, leaving smaller organisations least equipped. These findings show that potential contamination cases are now a routine reality for ADOs, but the procedural tools to manage them are not. The evidence collected here will inform forthcoming Council of Europe's best-practice recommendations aimed at protecting athletes while preserving the integrity of clean sport.

title: Sustainable sport nutrition behaviors, mental resilience, and perceived athletic performance in competitive athletes
title_original: Sustainable sport nutrition behaviors, mental resilience, and perceived athletic performance in competitive athletes
summary: Background Sustainable dietary practices may influence athlete health, recovery, psychological stability, and environmental responsibility; however, evidence regarding their relationship with mental resilience and perceived athletic performance remains limited. Objective This study investigated associations among sustainable sport nutrition practices, sustainability awareness, recovery quality, mental resilience, and perceived athletic performance in competitive athletes. Methods A cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted over 8 weeks. Of 300 invited athletes, 230 agreed to participate and 202 completed the full survey. Participants completed self-report measures assessing sustainable sport nutrition practices, sustainability awareness, recovery quality, mental resilience, and perceived athletic performance. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 survey completers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression, while qualitative data were examined using reflexive thematic analysis and integrated through a joint display. Results Sustainable sport nutrition practices were positively associated with mental resilience ( r = 0.47, p < 0.001), recovery quality ( r = 0.43, p < 0.001), and perceived athletic performance ( r = 0.39, p < 0.001). Sustainability awareness was associated with sustainable nutrition practices ( r = 0.51, p < 0.001). title: Traditional Chinese health-preserving exercises and self-worth in older adults: a moderated mediation model
title_original: Traditional Chinese health-preserving exercises and self-worth in older adults: a moderated mediation model
summary: Objective This study examined the association between traditional Chinese health-preserving exercises and self-worth in older adults, focusing on the mediating role of self-identity and the moderating role of social support. Method A cluster sampling approach was adopted to recruit 500 older adults from 12 representative Tai Chi and Health Qigong associations in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area for a cross-sectional survey. Data were collected using the Traditional Chinese Health-Preserving Exercise Scale, the Self-Identity Scale, the Social Support Scale, and the Self-Worth Scale. Amos 26.0 was used to assess the reliability and validity of the scales. SPSS 27.0 was employed to conduct descriptive statistics and correlation analyses for the four variables, followed by multiple linear regression to examine the total association. Subsequently, the SPSS PROCESS macro (Models 4 and 7) was used to test the mediating role of self-identity and the moderated mediation model, respectively. Results Significant positive correlations were observed between any two of the four variables: traditional Chinese health-preserving exercises, self-identity, social support, and self-worth ( p < 0.01). Multiple linear regression analysis showed that traditional Chinese health-preserving exercises were significantly and positively associated with self-worth ( β = 0.104, p < 0.05). The indirect pathway from traditional Chinese health-preserving exercises to self-worth through self-identity was significant [ β = 0.095, Bootstrap 95% CI (0.018, 0.165)]. Moreover, social support moderated the association between traditional Chinese health-preserving exercises and self-identity, which was strongest at high levels of social support ( β = 0.365, p < 0.001), and the mediating role of self-identity was significant only at high levels of social support [ β = 0.143, Bootstrap 95% CI (0.052, 0.231)]. Conclusion Drawing on the theoretical frameworks of self-worth, self-identity, and social support, this study suggests that among older adults who enjoy robust social support networks, regular engagement in traditional Chinese health-preserving exercises is associated with the development and reinforcement of self-identity across physiological, psychological, and social dimensions. Within this process, older adults may become increasingly oriented toward contemplating the meaning of life in a natural context, shifting from a focus on external achievements toward exploring inner peace and the inherent value of life, and this reorientation may accompany the fulfillment of self-worth.

title: Motivation and Constraints in Recreation Participation Among Children and Adults With Disabilities
title_original: Motivation and Constraints in Recreation Participation Among Children and Adults With Disabilities
summary: This dissertation investigated how motivation and constraints relate to participation in outdoor and community recreation among children with disabilities and adults who are blind or visually impaired. Although outdoor recreation is associated with important physical, psychological, and social benefits, people with disabilities continue to participate at lower rates than their peers without disabilities, and prior work shows that barriers extend well beyond physical access to include structural, interpersonal, and intrapersonal constraints. Drawing on the Constraint–Negotiation Model (CNM) and social cognitive theory, this dissertation addressed gaps in multivariate research and life-course perspectives by examining whether and how motivations, perceived constraints, and participation are linked in two distinct but complementary populations. Study 1 used a cross-sectional online survey of parents and guardians of children with disabilities who are customers of a large Mid-Atlantic municipal park system. Parents reported consistently high motivation across achievement, social, and nature domains, and these motivational orientations were broadly similar across demographic groups. However, neither demographic characteristics nor motivation subscales significantly predicted 30-day facility use, revealing a clear disconnect between strong parental endorsement of recreation benefits and actual utilization. Study 2 surveyed adults who are blind or visually impaired across North America about their motivations, perceived intrapersonal, interpersonal, and structural constraints, participation in outdoor recreation, and health-related quality of life. Participants reported moderate motivation and moderate constraints, with constraint subscales strongly interrelated. That is, structural constraints showed modest negative associations with participation, and intrapersonal and structural constraints had small negative associations with health-related quality of life. In contrast, motivation and participation frequency had low correlation with health outcomes. Taken together, the studies suggested that motivation is not the primary limiting factor in these disability contexts. Instead, persistent structural, interpersonal, and intrapersonal barriers were more consequential for both participation and well-being. Theoretically, the findings extended CNM and social cognitive perspectives by underscoring the need to incorporate negotiation-efficacy, perceptions of environmental predictability, and the cumulative psychological impact of repeated exposure to barriers. Practically, the results pointed toward organizational and environmental changes, rather than attempts to “boost” already high motivation, as the most promising pathways to more equitable participation. Recommended priorities included improving the accessibility of facilities and programs, expanding adapted equipment and transportation options, enhancing staff disability competence and inclusive communication, partnering with families and adults with visual impairments to co-design programs, and creating socially supportive, group-based opportunities. Across the lifespan, reducing constraints and strengthening support for negotiation appeared essential for translating motivation into meaningful, sustained engagement in outdoor and community recreation for people with disabilities.

title: Building smarter surveillance: a framework for artificial intelligence-enabled monitoring of overuse injuries in youth sports
title_original: Building smarter surveillance: a framework for artificial intelligence-enabled monitoring of overuse injuries in youth sports
summary: Early sport specialization (ESS), defined as intensive, year-round training in a single sport at the exclusion of others, has become increasingly prevalent among youth athletes. This trend has coincided with a rise in overuse injuries, and premature attrition. Concurrently, advances in wearable sensors and artificial intelligence (AI) enable real-time quantification of training load, biomechanical deviations, and recovery. However, a translational gap remains: existing AI surveillance models are predominantly validated in elite adult male cohorts, leaving youth athletes underserved. To address this gap, we propose a translational four-pillar framework for ESS-aware AI injury monitoring in youth sport. Bridging technological capabilities with developmental physiology through structured AI surveillance provides a structured risk-monitoring roadmap with the potential to inform preventative strategies, optimize physical readiness, and support long-term musculoskeletal health in youth athletes.

title: The paradox of protection: rethinking challenge, wellbeing, and development in high-performance sport
title_original: The paradox of protection: rethinking challenge, wellbeing, and development in high-performance sport
summary: Over recent decades, sport psychology has undergone an important and largely welcome shift towards athlete wellbeing, mental health, and safeguarding. International consensus frameworks have rightly emphasised the need to recognise psychological distress, improve access to support, and protect athletes from unnecessary harm (Reardon et al., 2026). This conversation has become increasingly sophisticated, recognising that athlete wellbeing is shaped by relationships, organisational cultures, and the broader performance environment (Purcell et al., 2019;Küttel & Larsen, 2020). These developments represent important progress.We suggest that sport psychology has become more sophisticated in identifying the risks of excessive challenge than the developmental risks of insufficient challenge. Because harm is often immediate and visible, while the costs of under-challenge may emerge only later, policy and practice may default too readily towards reducing difficult demands. This risks treating discomfort as a problem to be alleviated rather than a potential feature of ambitious development.Discomfort, distress, and harm are not equivalent. Some psychological unpleasantness may be developmentally desirable because athletes cannot develop capacities for uncertainty, difficult emotion, failure, or pressure without encountering those demands. The task is therefore to distinguish legitimate developmental challenge from avoidable harm, recognising that the balance between protection, support, and challenge will vary across athletes, circumstances, and stages of development. Accordingly, this paper examines challenge as a central mechanism of development, stress as a principal way challenge is psychologically experienced, and the implications of both for psychological support. We argue that sport psychology should keep athletes safe from harm without making them safe from the challenges through which ambitious development occurs.Progress in high-performance sport requires athletes to adapt when their existing capacities no longer meet emerging demands. Development rarely occurs through uninterrupted success; athletes encounter uncertainty, failure, deselection, injury, competitive pressure, and emotional disruption that require them to reconsider and refine how they perform (Collins et al., 2016). Here, development refers to an enduring expansion or reorganisation of psychological, behavioural, or technical capacities. Challenge creates the discrepancy between what an athlete can currently manage and what future performance requires. Without that discrepancy, there is little impetus for adaptation and limited opportunity for development (Taylor et al., 2022).Challenge is not the same as unnecessary adversity or avoidable harm. Exposure to difficulty does not guarantee growth, and subsequent success cannot justify inappropriate practice, even in hindsight. However, high-performance development necessarily involves demands that are uncomfortable and sometimes genuinely distressing. When such demands are proportionate, developmentally relevant, and accompanied by appropriate support and recovery, the disruption they create can prompt learning and adaptation (Kong et al., 2025).Some forms of psychological unpleasantness may therefore be developmentally desirable, rather than merely unavoidable. Athletes cannot learn to tolerate uncertainty without experiencing it, regulate difficult emotions without encountering them, or develop the capacity to perform under pressure without practising under pressure (Bouthiller & Lautenbach, 2025). In these circumstances, discomfort is not simply an unwanted by-product of development; it forms part of the developmental stimulus because it provides the context in which the relevant capacities are exercised. As such, removing the discomfort may also remove the opportunity for those capacities to develop. Its developmental value lies in what the experience requires of the athlete and how that experience is structured and supported (Kong et al., 2025).Intensity alone cannot determine whether a demand promotes development or becomes overwhelming. It also depends on how the athlete appraises the demand and the resources available to meet it (Lazarus, 1991). Athletes' experiences of challenge are shaped by their existing capacities, previous experiences, and access to appropriate support (Williams & MacNamara, 2022). Appraisal may also change through perceived control, relationships, and interaction with the wider performance environment (Bonetti & Hauw, 2026). The same demand may therefore be manageable for one athlete, overwhelming for another, or experienced differently by the same athlete over time.Challenge is consequently best understood as a dynamic relationship between the athlete, the demand, and the performance environment. Development depends not on removing difficulty, but on enabling athletes to engage with, adapt to, and make sense of demanding experiences in ways that expand their capacities.Recognising challenge as a mechanism of development does not mean that all demanding experiences are beneficial. Distress refers here to the unpleasant psychological experience that may accompany demanding circumstances, whereas harm involves a significant adverse effect on an athlete's health, safety, dignity, functioning, or longer-term development. The two may overlap, but they are not synonymous: athletes may experience distress without harm, while harm may develop without immediate distress. Wellbeing therefore means more than the absence of discomfort; it concerns athletes' capacity to function, develop, and pursue meaningful goals without unacceptable costs (Reardon et al., 2026). Safeguarding involves (or at least should) preventing practices and environments that threaten these conditions (Tuakli-Wosornu et al., 2024).The boundary between developmental challenge and avoidable harm is not fixed. It depends on the purpose and proportionality of the demand, the athlete's appraisal, available resources and support, and the consequences over time. A legitimate challenge may become harmful when demands are excessive or accumulate without adequate recovery, when athletes experience persistent helplessness or impairment, or when exposure continues despite deteriorating health. Research on burnout similarly highlights the interaction between demands, recovery, motivation, and the performance environment, rather than treating stressful experiences as inherently harmful (Woods et al., 2025).Power and agency also matter. Although athletes cannot choose every training demand, performance standard, or selection decision, they should understand the purpose of a demand, be able to express concerns, and be able to report inappropriate practice without fear of disproportionate consequences. How demands are imposed may matter as much as the demands themselves: controlling environments have been associated with psychological need thwarting (Bartholomew et al., 2011) and athlete burnout (Barcza-Renner et al., 2016). Younger athletes require greater caution, as their dependence on adults may limit their capacity to challenge demanding practices (Bergeron et al., 2024). Neither a coach's developmental intention nor an athlete's apparent acceptance is sufficient to establish that a practice is appropriate. Equally, temporary discomfort is not sufficient evidence of harm. It may require adjusting the intensity, timing, duration, or support around a challenge rather than removing it. However, when health, safety, dignity, functioning, or longer-term development are threatened, protection from harm takes priority.If challenge creates the conditions for development, stress is one of the main ways challenge is psychologically experienced. High-performance demands often generate stress because athletes pursue goals that matter deeply to them. Its presence does not therefore necessarily indicate dysfunction or that something has gone wrong. Indeed, for many it may be of long duration. The more important distinction is between the expected stress of engaging with meaningful demands and stress that becomes persistent, impairing, or harmful (Reardon et al., 2026).The significance of stress depends on how it is appraised and how it develops over time. Lazarus' (1991) transactional model conceptualises stress as a dynamic relationship between the demands an individual encounters and their appraisal of the resources available to meet them. Apparently similar situations may therefore produce markedly different responses. One athlete may experience a selection decision, serious injury, or major competition as manageable and meaningful, while another may find it overwhelming. These responses may also change as demands accumulate, resources diminish, or capacities develop through experience.Challenge and threat theory further supports this position. When athletes appraise their resources as sufficient to meet situational demands, they are more likely to experience a challenge state (Blascovich, 2008). In sport, challenge states have been associated with more adaptive physiological responses, attentional control, and performance under pressure, whereas threat becomes more likely when perceived demands exceed available resources (Jones et al., 2009). Neither response is a fixed property of the event or the athlete. Appraisal is continually shaped by previous experience, perceived control, relationships, and interaction with the performance environment (Bonetti & Hauw, 2026).Importantly, the aim cannot be to eliminate stress from the preparation for high-performance sport.Athletes are unlikely to develop the capacity to perform under pressure if training consistently protects them from experiencing it (Bouthiller & Lautenbach, 2025). Appropriate exposure allows athletes to practise interpreting, regulating, and responding to stress before encountering comparable demands in competition. Removing stress indiscriminately may therefore reduce immediate discomfort while also limiting preparation for future demands.The relevant question is not whether stress is good or bad, but what it signifies for this athlete, in this context, at this point in their development. For practitioners, this shifts the focus from routinely reducing stress to assessing and monitoring it. Psychological support should intervene when stress becomes overwhelming, persistent, or impairing, while helping athletes engage constructively with the pressures through which high-level capacities are developed.How psychological support is understood may shape whether athletes and coaches regard it as relevant to high performance. In cultures where toughness is associated with competence, seeking support may be interpreted as evidence of vulnerability or an inability to cope. Athletes may also worry that addressing distress will diminish their motivation, competitive edge, or capacity to tolerate pressure. Alongside concerns about stigma, confidentiality, and career consequences, these perceptions may discourage help-seeking (Gulliver et al., 2012).Such concerns may reflect uncertainty about the purpose of psychological support. If psychology is understood primarily as reducing discomfort, those who regard challenge as integral to performance may question its value. Psychological support should also help athletes engage effectively with demanding experiences by appraising challenges accurately and regulating difficult emotions (Lazarus, 1991), recovering appropriately, and making meaning from disruption (Taylor et al., 2022). Practitioners can strengthen athlete agency and help coaches calibrate, explain, and support legitimate challenge (Kong et al., 2025). They should also monitor whether stress is becoming cumulative or impairing (Edwards & Weatherbee, 2026). Where there are signs of harm, maltreatment, or significant deterioration, protection and appropriate intervention take priority (Tuakli-Wosornu et al., 2024). Where challenge remains proportionate, support should help athletes remain engaged long enough for adaptation and learning to occur.The aim is not to eliminate stress or encourage it indiscriminately, but to help athletes engage constructively with legitimate challenge while recognising when intervention is required. Wellbeing and development should be advanced together, although they need not receive identical emphasis in every situation or at every developmental stage. Wellbeing is not synonymous with comfort, and discomfort is not, by itself, evidence of harm.The growing emphasis on wellbeing and safeguarding has delivered important progress. However, it has also left the developmental significance of difficult and unpleasant experiences comparatively under-specified. High-performance development involves uncertainty, failure, pressure, vulnerability, and emotional disruption. Although these experiences are not inherently beneficial, discomfort and distress are not necessarily evidence of harm. Some forms of unpleasantness are developmentally desirable because they provide the conditions in which athletes exercise and extend the capacities required for ambitious performance.Rebalancing wellbeing and development requires more than asserting that both matter. It requires recognising that they will not always receive equal emphasis and that the appropriate balance will vary across athletes, contexts, and stages of development. There is also a need to acknowledge and redress the 'concept creep' which has seen many psychological constructs uncritically expanded to incorporate completely different or more moderate forms of the original (Haslam, 2016). At times, protection and recovery should take priority. At other times, however, development may require athletes to encounter and work through demands that temporarily unsettle their wellbeing. Treating the reduction of discomfort as the default response risks protecting athletes from the very experiences high-performance sport requires them to be prepared for.Sport psychology must therefore distinguish avoidable harm from legitimate developmental challenge by attending to the athlete, the demand, the performance environment, and the consequences that emerge over time. Protection from harm remains fundamental, but it should not become protection from difficulty. The future of sport psychology lies in keeping athletes safe from harm while preparing them for, rather than shielding them from, the challenges through which ambitious development occurs.

Psychological support should intervene when stress becomes overwhelming, persistent, or impairing, while helping athletes engage constructively with the pressures through which high-level capacities are developed.How psychological support is understood may shape whether athletes and coaches regard it as relevant to high performance. In cultures where toughness is associated with competence, seeking support may be interpreted as evidence of vulnerability or an inability to cope. Athletes may also worry that addressing distress will diminish their motivation, competitive edge, or capacity to tolerate pressure. Alongside concerns about stigma, confidentiality, and career consequences, these perceptions may discourage help-seeking (Gulliver et al., 2012).Such concerns may reflect uncertainty about the purpose of psychological support. If psychology is understood primarily as reducing discomfort, those who regard challenge as integral to performance may question its value. Psychological support should also help athletes engage effectively with demanding experiences by appraising challenges accurately and regulating difficult emotions (Lazarus, 1991), recovering appropriately, and making meaning from disruption (Taylor et al., 2022). Practitioners can strengthen athlete agency and help coaches calibrate, explain, and support legitimate challenge (Kong et al., 2025). They should also monitor whether stress is becoming cumulative or impairing (Edwards & Weatherbee, 2026). Where there are signs of harm, maltreatment, or significant deterioration, protection and appropriate intervention take priority (Tuakli-Wosornu et al., 2024). Where challenge remains proportionate, support should help athletes remain engaged long enough for adaptation and learning to occur.The aim is not to eliminate stress or encourage it indiscriminately, but to help athletes engage constructively with legitimate challenge while recognising when intervention is required. Wellbeing and development should be advanced together, although they need not receive identical emphasis in every situation or at every developmental stage. Wellbeing is not synonymous with comfort, and discomfort is not, by itself, evidence of harm.The growing emphasis on wellbeing and safeguarding has delivered important progress. However, it has also left the developmental significance of difficult and unpleasant experiences comparatively under-specified. High-performance development involves uncertainty, failure, pressure, vulnerability, and emotional disruption. Although these experiences are not inherently beneficial, discomfort and distress are not necessarily evidence of harm. Some forms of unpleasantness are developmentally desirable because they provide the conditions in which athletes exercise and extend the capacities required for ambitious performance.Rebalancing wellbeing and development requires more than asserting that both matter. It requires recognising that they will not always receive equal emphasis and that the appropriate balance will vary across athletes, contexts, and stages of development. There is also a need to acknowledge and redress the 'concept creep' which has seen many psychological constructs uncritically expanded to incorporate completely different or more moderate forms of the original (Haslam, 2016). At times, protection and recovery should take priority. At other times, however, development may require athletes to encounter and work through demands that temporarily unsettle their wellbeing. Treating the reduction of discomfort as the default response risks protecting athletes from the very experiences high-performance sport requires them to be prepared for.Sport psychology must therefore distinguish avoidable harm from legitimate developmental challenge by attending to the athlete, the demand, the performance environment, and the consequences that emerge over time. Protection from harm remains fundamental, but it should not become protection from difficulty. The future of sport psychology lies in keeping athletes safe from harm while preparing them for, rather than shielding them from, the challenges through which ambitious development occurs.

title: Effect of tangeretin supplements on simulated precompetition weight loss in female combat sports athletes
title_original: Effect of tangeretin supplements on simulated precompetition weight loss in female combat sports athletes
summary: Background Weight reduction before competition has long been a major challenge for combat-sports athletes. Unscientific weight-loss practices not only increase the risk of hormonal imbalance, electrolyte disturbance, and impaired immune function but also compromise athletic capacities such as aerobic and anaerobic performance and explosive power. This study investigated the potential benefits of tangeretin, a natural citrus extract, on athletic performance. These benefits include the regulation of hormone secretion, the optimization of carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, and the promotion of muscle synthesis and lipid utilization, which may help athletes reach their target weight.Objective To examine the effects of tangeretin supplementation on body-composition and sports-performance indicators in female combat-sports athletes, and to evaluate its efficacy for simulated precompetition weight loss.Methods Thirty female combat-sports athletes (4 wrestlers, 3 boxers, 9 sanda athletes, 3 judokas, and 11 taekwondo athletes) were recruited. A paired, randomized, double-blind design was used. All 30 participants were first paired according to sport and competitive level, then randomly allocated to either a tangeretin group or a placebo group (15 per group). The 30-day intervention comprised a double-blind nutritional supplement, a dietary questionnaire, blood sampling and analysis, body-composition assessment, isokinetic muscle-strength testing, and aerobic-capacity testing, to evaluate the effects of tangeretin (400 mg/day) on performance and health-related outcomes. These outcomes included body-composition indicators (e.g. body-fat percentage, fat mass, lean-body mass), fat-distribution indicators (e.g. limb and regional fat mass, gynoid fat mass), glucose and lipid-metabolism indicators (e.g. LDL-C, total cholesterol, free fatty acids), hormone indicators (e.g. cortisol, testosterone), muscle-strength indicators (e.g. peak torque of hip, knee, and ankle flexors and extensors), and maximal-oxygen-uptake-derived indicators (e.g. VO2max heart rate, time to exhaustion). Statistical significance was assessed using two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA).Results (1) Body weight: 80.0% of athletes in the tangeretin group lost weight to varying degrees, and 33.3% (5 athletes) reached their competition weight class. (2) Body fat: body-fat percentage in the tangeretin group decreased from 23.92 ± 0.87% to 22.92 ± 0.89%; trunk, upper-limb, lower-limb, and android-region fat mass decreased by 6.77%, 8.77%, 4.43%, and 8.09%, respectively. (3) Glucose and lipid metabolism: HDL-C increased by 8.86% (P = 0.002), whereas triglycerides decreased by 25.00% (P = 0.048). (4) Sports performance: peak torque during hip, knee, and ankle flexion and extension increased significantly in the tangeretin group. VO2max also improved from 42.80 ± 1.13 to 43.46 ± 1.32 ml/kg/min.Conclusion Tangeretin supplementation effectively reduced body weight and fat mass (both overall and regionally) in female combat-sports athletes. Among the participants, 80.0% lost weight to varying degrees, and 33.3% reached their competition weight class, indicating a strong effect on precompetition weight loss. Moreover, tangeretin improved aerobic capacity and lower-limb joint muscle strength, thereby enhancing competitive performance.

title: ДИФЕРЕНЦІЙОВАНИЙ АЛГОРИТМ ЛАБОРАТОРНОГО МОНІТОРИНГУ В ПРОЦЕСІ ЗАНЯТЬ СТАРШОКЛАСНИКІВ СХІДНИМИ БОЙОВИМИ МИСТЕЦТВАМИ ТА ЄДИНОБОРСТВАМИ
title_original: ДИФЕРЕНЦІЙОВАНИЙ АЛГОРИТМ ЛАБОРАТОРНОГО МОНІТОРИНГУ В ПРОЦЕСІ ЗАНЯТЬ СТАРШОКЛАСНИКІВ СХІДНИМИ БОЙОВИМИ МИСТЕЦТВАМИ ТА ЄДИНОБОРСТВАМИ
summary: Актуальність проблеми зумовлена поєднанням фізичних і психоемоційних навантажень із незавершеністю морфофункціонального дозрівання організму в пізньому підлітковому віці, а також недостатньою представленістю у науковій літературі цілісних алгоритмів лабораторного контролю цієї категорії осіб. У статті обґрунтовано концепцію диференційованого лабораторного моніторингу функціонального стану старшокласників, які систематично займаються східними єдиноборствами. Мета дослідження − розробка для впровадження в контроль здоровʼя старшокласників, які систематично займаються східними єдиноборствами та бойовими мистецтвами, диференційованого алгоритму лабораторного моніторингу адаптаційних процесів, спрямованого на своєчасне виявлення і профілактику несприятливих змін організму. Методологію роботи становили концептуально-аналітичний підхід, систематизація даних сучасної спортивної медицини, педіатрії, лабораторної діагностики, теорії та методики підготовки спортсменів, а також структурно-функціональне моделювання послідовності діагностичних рішень. Результати. У статті обґрунтовано концепцію диференційованого лабораторного моніторингу функціонального стану старшокласників, які систематично займаються східними єдиноборствами. Запропоновано трирівневу систему моніторингу: базовий вихідний скринінг, плановий контроль адаптації та поглиблене обстеження за клінічними або тренувальними показаннями. Визначено принципи добору лабораторних показників, стандартизації переданалітичного етапу, інтерпретації індивідуальної динаміки та розмежування компетенцій учителя, тренера і лікаря. До базового профілю включено загальноклінічні, гематологічні, стандартні біохімічні показники та аналіз сечі; до планового − параметри еритропоезу й обміну заліза, функціонального стану печінки та нирок, адекватності адаптації до фізичного навантаження і системного запалення; до поглибленого − електролітний, ендокринний, кістково-метаболічний та інші спеціалізовані блоки, а за необхідності − визначення біомаркерів функціонального стану серця та пошкодження скелетних м’язів, зокрема синдромів EIMD і DOMS. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає у створенні багаторівневої моделі, що поєднує вікову доцільність, індивідуалізацію, етапність і клінічну безпеку. Результати. Запропонований алгоритм лабораторної діагностики дає можливість його використання як основи для організації медико-біологічного супроводу старшокласників, які займаються східними єдиноборствами, та подальшої проспективної апробації.

title: Olympic fencing medallists are increasingly clustering around an age that has hardly changed (1896–2024)
title_original: Olympic fencing medallists are increasingly clustering around an age that has hardly changed (1896–2024)
summary: Fencing has been contested at every modern Olympic Games since 1896, giving it one of the longest continuous records in sports and an opportunity to examine whether an optimal age at medal-winning exists and whether it has changed. We examined every individual Olympic fencing medallist from 1896 to 2024, resulting in 379 medals won by 286 athletes across foil, épée, and sabre. Of these, the available birth date records of 282 athletes (>95% of the total) were retained, resulting in 375 medals with a date of birth resolved to the day of each event, and the analyses based on those. Across the full 128 years, the average medallist was 28.8 years old, and gold, silver, and bronze medallists were the same age as one another ( p = 0.195). The mean age of male medallists changed little, falling by approximately one-third of a year per decade ( p = 0.006), with no discontinuity at the end of the amateur era in 1972. However, the change pertained to the range of ages rather than the mean. Early medallists ranged from 16.8 to 50.0 years, and no male athlete has won an Olympic fencing medal beyond the age of 42 in the past 50 years. Ages were approximately 1.5 times as variable before 1972 as after it, and the narrowing occurred in foil, épée, and sabre alike. In the past two decades, the age of medal winners was concentrated in a narrow band: the mean age of medal winners was 27.7 years, and 50% all medals were won between 24.1 and 30.8 years. That band was similar across foil, épée, and sabre, and similar for women and men. Among Olympic medallists, therefore, the age at which the medals are won has not shifted; what has diminished is the winning of medals far from it. However, whether the same holds below the podium is not addressed by these data.

title: The fast–slow stretch-shortening cycle classification: provenance, transmission and evidential status of the 250 ms boundary
title_original: The fast–slow stretch-shortening cycle classification: provenance, transmission and evidential status of the 250 ms boundary
summary: Ground contact time is widely used to classify plyometric exercises as fast (< approximately 250 ms) or slow (> approximately 250 ms) stretch-shortening cycle (SSC) actions, shaping drill selection, progression and study design in training and rehabilitation. A categorical threshold is informative only if it marks a reproducible change in mechanism, in outcome, or in decision value, defined here as its capacity to change a prescription decision such as drill selection or progression. We examine the source of the 250 ms boundary, its original criteria, the evidence for a mechanistic breakpoint, what contact time indexes mechanically, the determinants of category membership, and the consequences for prescription and synthesis. In the source, long and short SSC actions were defined using two joint conditions, movement duration and angular displacement at the hip, knee and ankle, and the short category was bounded between 100 and 250 ms. This definition was subsequently reduced in much of the research literature to a one-sided ground-contact-time threshold without documented validation, whereas both criteria were often retained in applied accounts. The only direct test, in 46 recreationally active men, did not reproduce 250 ms and identified Achilles tendon length as the strongest discriminator of contact-time groups. Existing mechanistic evidence distinguishes slow from fast tasks but does not identify a discontinuity at 250 ms. In vivo and impulse–momentum evidence shows instead that contact time indexes how a required impulse is delivered and how length change is partitioned between tendon and muscle, and that both vary continuously with task constraints. In parallel, common intensity metrics rank drills differently, and fast SSC drills have contact times two to three times longer than a sprint contact. In rehabilitation the boundary is used as an injury-dependent progression gate, and meta-analyses have not been stratified by the criterion used to assign categories. These findings do not establish that 250 ms is useless; they show that it should be treated as an unvalidated operational heuristic rather than a biologically privileged boundary. Its value should be tested prospectively by asking whether category membership predicts training response once tendon geometry, task and measurement are accounted for.

title: “ENHANCED GAMES” ЯК ВИКЛИК АНТИДОПІНГОВОМУ УПРАВЛІННЮ У СПОРТІ
title_original: “ENHANCED GAMES” ЯК ВИКЛИК АНТИДОПІНГОВОМУ УПРАВЛІННЮ У СПОРТІ
summary: Актуальність проблеми. Проведення 24 травня 2026 р. у Лас-Вегасі перших “The Enhanced Games” (TEG), у яких дозволено використання більшості речовин із Забороненого списку Всесвітнього антидопінгового агентства (ВАДА) під медичним наглядом, актуалізувало дискусію про ефективність, легітимність і майбутнє глобальної антидопінгової системи. Феномен TEG розглянуто не лише як провокаційну спортивну подію, а як прояв накопичених суперечностей у діяльності ВАДА та нову модель комерціалізації фармакологічного вдосконалення людини. Мета дослідження – здійснити комплексний аналіз передумов виникнення TEG, аргументів їх прихильників і противників, спортивних, медичних, фінансових та управлінських наслідків першого проведення змагань, а також визначити виклики для спортивних організацій різних рівнів. Методи дослідження. Застосовано систематичний огляд літератури, порівняльний аналіз, метод кейс-стаді, синтез і узагальнення, документальний аналіз. Результати дослідження. Систематизовано чотири кластери критики антидопінгової системи: ліберально-філософський, правовий, науковий та управлінський. Установлено, що TEG використовують концепцію «зниження шкоди» як альтернативу заборонній моделі, однак її практична реалізація не має достатньої доказової бази щодо безпеки суперфізіологічних доз препаратів, а організатори не оприлюднили даних медичного моніторингу учасників. Виявлено невідповідність між комерційною риторикою проєкту та результатами дебютних змагань: у 23 дисциплінах лише один результат був швидшим за чинний світовий рекорд, тоді як акції материнської компанії після події втратили близько 70 % вартості. Запропоновано типологію управлінських викликів для ВАДА і МОК, міжнародних федерацій, національних антидопінгових організацій, клубів, тренерів та медичного персоналу. Показано, що реакція спортивного руху на TEG перейшла від публічного засудження до організаційних і правових заходів, зокрема обмежень з боку Міжнародної федерації плавання (World Aquatics) та судового протистояння між організаторами TEG і ВАДА. Визначено практичні імплікації для НАДЦУ з урахуванням участі українського спортсмена. Обґрунтовано необхідність поєднання захисту здоров’я спортсменів, процесуальної справедливості та науково обґрунтованого перегляду антидопінгової політики.

title: INCIDÊNCIA DE MARCAÇÕES DE DUPLO CONTATO: UMA ANÁLISE EM PARTIDAS DE VOLEIBOL DOS JOGOS OLÍMPICOS DE PARIS 2024
title_original: INCIDÊNCIA DE MARCAÇÕES DE DUPLO CONTATO: UMA ANÁLISE EM PARTIDAS DE VOLEIBOL DOS JOGOS OLÍMPICOS DE PARIS 2024
summary: Objetivo: O presente estudo teve como objetivo analisar a incidência de marcações da regra do duplo contato realizadas pela arbitragem durante as fases finais das partidas de voleibol masculino e feminino dos Jogos Olímpicos de Paris 2024. Métodos: Foi realizada uma pesquisa descritiva, de abordagem quantitativa e caráter observacional, por meio da análise de vídeos de oito partidas de voleibol de alto rendimento, sendo quatro do torneio feminino e quatro do masculino, correspondentes às semifinais, disputas pelo terceiro lugar e finais. Foram registradas exclusivamente as situações em que a arbitragem assinalou oficialmente a infração de duplo contato, sendo os dados organizados em tabelas para posterior análise descritiva. Resultados: Os resultados demonstraram que não foram identificadas marcações oficiais de duplo contato pela arbitragem nas oito partidas analisadas, correspondendo a uma incidência de 0%. Conclusão: Conclui-se que, nas partidas que compuseram a amostra, não houve marcações oficiais da infração de duplo contato pela arbitragem, indicando ausência de ocorrências dessa penalização nas fases finais analisadas dos Jogos Olímpicos de Paris 2024.

title: Positional Competition and Position-Specific Demands: Their Interaction and Association with Sport-Related Anxiety in Collegiate Athletes
title_original: Positional Competition and Position-Specific Demands: Their Interaction and Association with Sport-Related Anxiety in Collegiate Athletes
summary: The present study examines the difference in anxiety levels between individual sport athletes, team sport athletes, and dual-stress athletes -athletes in team sports who experience high position-specific demands as well as high positional competition.Guided by the Theory of Challenge and Threat States in Athletes (TCTSA), the study investigated whether the compounded stressors associated with certain team-sport positions would elevate anxiety levels.Using the Sport Anxiety Scale-2 (SAS-2), anxiety was measured across somatic, worry, and concentration disruption subscales.Ninety-seven collegiate athletes were recruited.Results discovered that dual-stress athletes reported lower concentration disruption but higher perceived positional competitiveness than individual sport athletes.These findings highlight the distinctive nature of dual-stress athletes and suggest the heightened coping mechanisms needed to perform and navigate the demands of their roles.

title: Data and materials for: Diagnostic effectiveness of the Sport Mental Health Assessment Tool 1 supplemented with a brief clinical intake interview in a cohort of Polish elite Olympic athletes
title_original: Data and materials for: Diagnostic effectiveness of the Sport Mental Health Assessment Tool 1 supplemented with a brief clinical intake interview in a cohort of Polish elite Olympic athletes
summary: Anonymised item-level data from 1121 elite Polish athletes from Olympic sports (545 female, 576 male), collected during routine biannual medical check-ups at the National Centre for Sports Medicine in Poland between 13 November 2023 and 4 June 2024, two to eight months before the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. The dataset includes the Polish adaptation of the IOC Sport Mental Health Assessment Tool 1 (SMHAT-1 forms 1 and 2: APSQ, GAD-7, PHQ-9, ASSQ, AUDIT-C, CAGE-AID, BEDA-Q) and mental health recommendations from brief clinical intake interviews with sport psychologists. These data underlie Waleriańczyk et al. (2025), British Journal of Sports Medicine, 59(1), 56–63, https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2024-108919, where they were originally published as online supplementary file 2. This research was funded by the National Science Centre, Poland (grant no. 2023/51/B/HS6/02835).

title: BUSINESS EDUCATION AS A FACTOR  IN INCREASING LABOR EFFICIENCY
title_original: BUSINESS EDUCATION AS A FACTOR  IN INCREASING LABOR EFFICIENCY
summary:
В статье рассматривается роль бизнес образования в повышении эффективности труда и сокращении трудовых затрат в организации. Автор анализирует современные тенденции спроса и предложения на рынке бизнес образования: переход от краткосрочных тренингов к системному и практико ориентированному обучению, рост востребованности командного развития, интерес к экономичным форматам обучения
                  The article examines the role of business education in increasing labor efficiency and reducing labor costs in an organization. The author analyzes current trends in demand and supply in the business education market, including the shift from short-term training to systematic and practice-oriented education, the growing demand for team development, and the interest in cost-effective learning formats

title: Верумика: онтологическая дихотомия справедливости и доказательство справедливости мироустройства
title_original: Верумика: онтологическая дихотомия справедливости и доказательство справедливости мироустройства
summary: В статье представлено формальное доказательство справедливости мироустройства, основанное на онтологической дихотомии справедливости и несправедливости. Вводится определение справедливости как точного соответствия воздаяния деянию (V = D). Доказывается, что справедливость онтологически неустойчива: любое нарушение порождает необратимый каскад, который в вечности доходит до предела. Из этого выводится онтологическая дихотомия: мир либо полностью справедлив, либо полностью несправедлив. Доказывается всеобщность антиверумизма в науке через анализ научных теорий (многомировая интерпретация Эверетта) и предлагается экспериментальное подтверждение через опрос учёных-физиков. Доказывается, что всеобщий антиверумизм возможен только в справедливом мире, что замыкает доказательство. Предлагается проверяемый прогноз: повышение личной честности учёных до уровня 50/50 должно приводить к смене антиверумического мировоззрения на верумическое.

title: ФИЗИЧЕСКАЯ КУЛЬТУРА И СПОРТ КАК ЭКОНОМИЧЕСКАЯ СИСТЕМА
title_original: ФИЗИЧЕСКАЯ КУЛЬТУРА И СПОРТ КАК ЭКОНОМИЧЕСКАЯ СИСТЕМА
summary:
Целью статьи является теоретическое обоснование физической культуры и спорта как экономической системы посредством выявления и применения признаков экономической системности, определения секторной и институциональной структуры, а также построения секторно-институциональной матрицы с последующим обоснованием её аналитических возможностей. Проблема исследования обусловлена фрагментарностью представлений и разобщённостью научных подходов к исследованию физической культуры и спорта, вследствие чего её социально-культурное содержание, экономические отношения, секторная организация, институциональная структура и механизмы воспроизводства преимущественно рассматриваются обособленно, что препятствует формированию целостного представления об анализируемой сфере и комплексному анализу процессов её функционирования, адаптации и воспроизводства. Научная новизна заключается в интеграции научных представлений об экономической системе физической культуры и спорта посредством выявления признаков экономической системности, определения секторной и институциональной структуры и построения секторно-институциональной аналитической матрицы. Методологическую основу исследования составили системный подход, методы анализа, синтеза, сопоставления, систематизации научных и нормативных источников. В результате исследования систематизированы десять признаков экономической системности, определены одиннадцать институтов, объединённых в четыре группы, и выделены государственный, некоммерческий и коммерческий сектора. На основе их сопоставления построена секторно-институциональная матрица, отражающая различия форм реализации институциональных механизмов в каждом секторе и позволяющая анализировать условия воспроизводства физкультурной и спортивной деятельности. Практическая значимость результатов заключается в возможности использования предложенной матрицы для анализа секторно-институциональной организации и механизмов воспроизводства сферы физической культуры и спорта. Полученные результаты формируют теоретико-методическую основу для дальнейшего исследования секторно-институциональной организации, процессов функционирования, адаптации и воспроизводства экономической системы физической культуры и спорта.
                  The article theoretically substantiates physical culture and sport as an economic system by identifying and applying the characteristics of economic systemic organization, determining its sectoral and institutional structure, and constructing a sector–institutional matrix with subsequent assessment of its analytical potential. The research problem stems from fragmented perspectives and insufficient integration of scholarly approaches to physical culture and sport. Consequently, its sociocultural content, economic relations, sectoral organization, institutional structure, and reproduction mechanisms are largely examined separately, which hinders a holistic understanding of the field and a comprehensive analysis of its functioning, adaptation, and reproduction. The scientific novelty lies in integrating theoretical perspectives on the economic system of physical culture and sport through identifying systemic economic characteristics, defining its sectoral and institutional structure, and developing a sector–institutional analytical matrix. The methodological framework combines the systems approach with analysis, synthesis, comparison, and systematization of scholarly and regulatory sources. The study systematizes ten characteristics of economic systemic organization, identifies eleven institutions grouped into four categories, and distinguishes public, nonprofit, and commercial sectors. Their comparison forms a sector–institutional matrix reflecting differences in the implementation of institutional mechanisms across sectors and enabling analysis of the conditions for reproducing physical culture and sports activities. The practical significance lies in the matrix’s applicability to analyzing sectoral–institutional organization and reproduction mechanisms. The findings provide a theoretical and methodological basis for further research into the functioning, adaptation, and reproduction of the economic system of physical culture and sport.

Научная новизна заключается в интеграции научных представлений об экономической системе физической культуры и спорта посредством выявления признаков экономической системности, определения секторной и институциональной структуры и построения секторно-институциональной аналитической матрицы. Методологическую основу исследования составили системный подход, методы анализа, синтеза, сопоставления, систематизации научных и нормативных источников. В результате исследования систематизированы десять признаков экономической системности, определены одиннадцать институтов, объединённых в четыре группы, и выделены государственный, некоммерческий и коммерческий сектора. На основе их сопоставления построена секторно-институциональная матрица, отражающая различия форм реализации институциональных механизмов в каждом секторе и позволяющая анализировать условия воспроизводства физкультурной и спортивной деятельности. Практическая значимость результатов заключается в возможности использования предложенной матрицы для анализа секторно-институциональной организации и механизмов воспроизводства сферы физической культуры и спорта. Полученные результаты формируют теоретико-методическую основу для дальнейшего исследования секторно-институциональной организации, процессов функционирования, адаптации и воспроизводства экономической системы физической культуры и спорта.
                  The article theoretically substantiates physical culture and sport as an economic system by identifying and applying the characteristics of economic systemic organization, determining its sectoral and institutional structure, and constructing a sector–institutional matrix with subsequent assessment of its analytical potential. The research problem stems from fragmented perspectives and insufficient integration of scholarly approaches to physical culture and sport. Consequently, its sociocultural content, economic relations, sectoral organization, institutional structure, and reproduction mechanisms are largely examined separately, which hinders a holistic understanding of the field and a comprehensive analysis of its functioning, adaptation, and reproduction. The scientific novelty lies in integrating theoretical perspectives on the economic system of physical culture and sport through identifying systemic economic characteristics, defining its sectoral and institutional structure, and developing a sector–institutional analytical matrix. The methodological framework combines the systems approach with analysis, synthesis, comparison, and systematization of scholarly and regulatory sources. The study systematizes ten characteristics of economic systemic organization, identifies eleven institutions grouped into four categories, and distinguishes public, nonprofit, and commercial sectors. Their comparison forms a sector–institutional matrix reflecting differences in the implementation of institutional mechanisms across sectors and enabling analysis of the conditions for reproducing physical culture and sports activities. The practical significance lies in the matrix’s applicability to analyzing sectoral–institutional organization and reproduction mechanisms. The findings provide a theoretical and methodological basis for further research into the functioning, adaptation, and reproduction of the economic system of physical culture and sport.

title: Asfalten-qatran-parafin çöküntülərinin nasos-kompressor borusunda əmələ gəlməsi və kimyəvi təsirinin qarşısının alınmasının bəzi nəticələri
title_original: Asfalten-qatran-parafin çöküntülərinin nasos-kompressor borusunda əmələ gəlməsi və kimyəvi təsirinin qarşısının alınmasının bəzi nəticələri
summary: Məqalədə neft quyularının istismarı zamanı nasos-kompressor borularında (NKB) asfalten-qatran-parafin çöküntülərinin (AQPÇ) əmələ gəlməsi prosesi və onların hasilata mənfi təsirinin qarşısının alınması yolları tədqiq edilmişdir. Quyuların istismar təcrübəsinin təhlili göstərmişdir ki, AQPÇ-nin əmələ gəlməsi xüsusilə neftin quyu ağzında temperaturu 28–36°C arasında dəyişən, azdebitli və az sulu quyularda daha intensiv xarakter daşıyır. Tədqiqatın məqsədi AQPÇ-nin əmələ gəlməsinə təsir edən əsas amillərin müəyyən edilməsi, onların qarşısının alınması və effektiv təmizlənməsi üsullarının qiymətləndirilməsidir. İşdə çöküntülərin əmələgəlmə mexanizmləri, hasil olunan məhsul axınına verilən kimyəvi reagentlərin sabit neft emulsiyalarının demulsifikasiyasına təsiri, həmçinin müasir təmizləmə texnologiyaları elmi-praktik baxımdan təhlil edilmişdir. Vyetnam yataqlarında aparılmış tədqiqatların nəticələri göstərmişdir ki, AQPÇ-nin biokimyəvi kompozisiyalar vasitəsilə təmizlənməsi ən səmərəli və perspektivli üsullardan biridir. Müəyyən edilmişdir ki, su-qaz-neft qarışığının dispersatorlarla işlənməsi maye sisteminin köpürmə qabiliyyətini artırır, qazlift üsulu ilə qaldırmanın effektivliyini yüksəldir, hasilatın sabitliyini təmin edir, avadanlığın istismar müddətini uzadır və enerji sərfiyyatını azaldır.

title: MARKAZIY OSIYODA OLIY TA’LIM: MOLIYALASHTIRISH VA INSTITUTSIONAL  TRANSFORMATSIYA
title_original: MARKAZIY OSIYODA OLIY TA’LIM: MOLIYALASHTIRISH VA INSTITUTSIONAL  TRANSFORMATSIYA
summary: This article provides a comparative analysis of the institutional and financial development of higher education systems in Central Asian countries, with particular emphasis on the structural changes observed in Uzbekistan during 2017-2025. Comparative, dynamic, and structural analyses show that the number of students increased 5.16-fold, while the number of higher education institutions nearly tripled. The development of higher education in Uzbekistan is conceptualized as a transition from limited access to institutional expansion and a diversified mass higher education system. Based on the findings, the study highlights the need to link higher education financing to quality and performance outcomes, incorporate risk assessment into student loan mechanisms, and evaluate non-state higher education institutions using outcome-based indicators.

title: МНОГОУРОВНЕВАЯ МОДЕЛЬ ИСПОЛЬЗОВАНИЯ ДАННЫХ ДЕМОНСТРАЦИОННОГО ЭКЗАМЕНА ДЛЯ ДИАГНОСТИКИ ПРОФЕССИОНАЛЬНЫХ ДЕФИЦИТОВ И УПРАВЛЕНИЯ КАЧЕСТВОМ ПОДГОТОВКИ БУХГАЛТЕРОВ СПО
title_original: МНОГОУРОВНЕВАЯ МОДЕЛЬ ИСПОЛЬЗОВАНИЯ ДАННЫХ ДЕМОНСТРАЦИОННОГО ЭКЗАМЕНА ДЛЯ ДИАГНОСТИКИ ПРОФЕССИОНАЛЬНЫХ ДЕФИЦИТОВ И УПРАВЛЕНИЯ КАЧЕСТВОМ ПОДГОТОВКИ БУХГАЛТЕРОВ СПО
summary: Статья посвящена разработке многоуровневой модели аналитического использования результатов демонстрационного экзамена по специальности 38.02.01 «Экономика и бухгалтерский учет (по отраслям)». Цель исследования — обосновать переход от интерпретации итогового суммарного балла к формированию диагностического профиля профессиональных дефицитов обучающихся. Эмпирическую базу составили обезличенные результаты демонстрационного экзамена трех образовательных организаций за 2024-2026 гг., а также материалы пилотного применения облачной учетной среды с фиксацией действий пользователей. Использованы методы сравнительного статистического, покритериального и функционально-технологического анализа. Установлено, что положительная итоговая отметка при компенсаторной агрегации баллов может не отражать несформированность отдельных критически значимых трудовых действий. Предложена пятиуровневая модель, объединяющая индивидуальный, групповой, организационный, региональный и федерально-отраслевой уровни работы с данными. Модель основана на сопоставлении цифрового следа экзаменующегося с эталоном контрольных показателей и может использоваться как дополнительный аналитико-диагностический контур без изменения установленного порядка государственной итоговой аттестации. Практическая значимость состоит в возможности адресной коррекции учебного процесса, образовательных программ и методической работы.
